messages.author: 97fe942905e4bb14
messages.subject: Setting up the DEC+J model
parts:
Hello, 

I am following the example script for the Psychotria phylogeny that was provided on the BioGeoBears website. When I am setting up the DEC+J model, I get these errors: 
> # Set up DEC+J model
> # Get the ML parameter values from the 2-parameter nested model
> # (this will ensure that the 3-parameter model always does at least as good)
> dstart = resDEC$outputs@params_table["d","est"]
Error: object 'resDEC' not found
> estart = resDEC$outputs@params_table["e","est"]
Error: object 'resDEC' not found
> jstart = 0.0001

Before this section, everything was going smoothly. I have the latest version of R and I installed all the latest versions of the packages required for BioGeoBears. 

What is "resDEC"? Am I supposed to upload a "params_table"? 

Thank you for your help!

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: Setting up the DEC+J model
parts:
Hi -- thanks for using the group.  "resDEC" stands for "results of DEC".  So you will have to run the DEC model first before running DEC+J, for those lines to work. You must have skipped that section.

That code is there so that the DEC+J search starts at the Maximum Likelihood Estimates (MLE) obtained under the DEC model.  This makes it easy to check if the DEC+J ML solution has a higher log-likelihood than the ML DEC solution.  Adding a parameter should always improve the log-likelihood, but if it doesn't, you have optimization failure (ML searches aren't always perfect).  This bit of code helps the user double-check.

However, if you don't want to run DEC first, just change those lines and pick your own starting values for d and e:

dstart = 0.01
estart = 0.01
jstart = 0.0001

Cheers, Nick
